messages:
maya: quick check — planning to flip the new canary for embeddings-route (project: search, model: embed-v2). Can someone confirm flag resolution order when there are overrides at org / project / route / model AND a force-off emergency flag? I remember there was a change last quarter.

leo: short answer: default order is model -> route -> project -> org (most specific wins). force-off is special: org-level force-off is evaluated after inheritance and will short-circuit to off if present.

sophia: small caveat: we added a `force` attribute on some flags in case a project wants to guarantee override even over model. It flips precedence between project and model when set. Not common but exists.

maya: ah okay — so force can invert precedence. Is there a clear way to tell which flags have `force:true`?

nate: there's a labeling convention in the flags UI and the API returns `meta.force: true`. Example API snippet: 
```json
GET /flags/search/embeddings-route
response: {"name":"emb_canary","scope":"route","meta":{"force":true}}
```

rachel: operational note: when you enable the canary, put a small audience (1%) and add guardrails (latency + quality). If org force-off exists it will still keep it off even if model & route say on.

maya: thanks. One more: if someone manually toggles a model-level flag via the console during the canary, does the rollout controller prefer the API state or the UI state?

leo: they are the same backing store — UI calls the API. However we do have a short-lived cache on the controller that can delay propagation (~30s). For emergency toggles we bypass cache.

sophia: FYI, deploy-bot will auto-revert a canary if the error-rate guardrail trips. It uses the effective resolved flag state at evaluation time.

deploy-bot: :warning: monitor: embeddings-route canary started at 1719005000, initial traffic 1%. Will abort if errors > 0.5% for 5m.

maya: perfect. I'll proceed but will ping here before flipping to 5% and attach the PR.

nate: pinging @rachel for guardrail thresholds, and @leo can you double-check `force` docs are in the flags README?

rachel: confirmed: latency + p99 < 1200ms, error-rate < 0.5%, quality regression < 0.8 BLEU drop. I'll post thresholds in the PR.

leo: will add `force` section to flags README and a short example. Also adding a lint to warn when both model-level `force:true` and org-level `force:true` exist (ambiguous).

maya: thanks all — proceeding with canary now, will update thread if anything unusual. :thumbsup:
